rca of the issue: Bug: POST /api/legitimacy/research returned HTTP 500 with pydantic ValidationError because the LegitimacyOut response model declared `user_id: str` as required (server.py class LegitimacyOut) but the endpoint constructed the response with `LegitimacyOut(**{k:v for k,v in doc.items() if k not in ('user_id','is_cache_seed','casino_name_lower')})` at line 1993 — the very field required by the schema was being stripped. Reproduction: any authenticated call to POST /api/legitimacy/research with any casino_name would 500. Fix: main agent removed the `user_id` field from the LegitimacyOut Pydantic model (lines 267-277) since the frontend never read it anyway. Verification: (a) live curl returns HTTP 200 with 10 expected keys and no user_id; (b) DB record still contains user_id (privacy invariant — reports are still attributed to a user for /history filtering, just not leaked in the response); (c) cache-hit path in the same endpoint (line 1892) uses the identical strip-then-construct pattern and also now returns 200; (d) /legitimacy/history calls LegitimacyOut(**d) directly on unstripped DB docs and still succeeds because pydantic v2 ignores extras by default. Mitigation for future regressions: consider adding `model_config = ConfigDict(extra='ignore')` explicitly to LegitimacyOut, or (better) drop the strip-dict-comprehension entirely at line 1892 and 1992 since pydantic already ignores extras — reduces two code paths that must stay in sync.
